title: Efficacy of prophylactic levetiracetam for improving functional outcome in the acute phase of intracerebral haemorrhage: a randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled, phase 3 trial PEACH 2
official: Efficacy of prophylactic levetiracetam for improving functional outcome in the acute phase of intracerebral haemorrhage: a randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled, phase 3 trial PEACH 2
summary: Main objective: to establish if primary prophylactic antiseizure drug improves functional outcome at 6 months in patients with ICH.

interventions.name: Keppra 100 mg/ml concentrate for solution for infusion

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. - Age ≥ 18 years
2. Spontaneous (non-traumatic) supratentorial intracerebral haemorrhage diagnosed by brain CT or MRI
3. Onset of neurologic symptoms within 24 hours
4. NIHSS score on admission ≤ 25
5. Informed consent given by the patient or his/her impartial witness
6. Patients benefiting from a social insurance system or a similar system
Exclusion criteria:
1. Intracerebral haemorrhage known or suspected by study investigator to be secondary to trauma, vascular malformation, haemorrhagic transformation of ischaemic stroke, or cerebral tumour
2. Patients with inaugural seizures at the onset of symptoms associated with intracerebral hemorrhage
3. Patients with QTc prolongation
4. Patients who have been part of a clinical study involving another investigational product in the previous 30 days or within 5 half-lives of the other investigational product prior to Screening, whichever is longer, or participant is currently receiving an investigational product
5. Patients taking probenecid, methotrexate or macrogol
6. Current use of antiseizure drugs or history of epilepsy
7. Severe renal insufficiency (creatinine clearance < 30 ml/min)
8. Pregnancy or breastfeeding
9. Previous history of severe depression, or psychotic disorder or suicidal attempt
10. - Known terminal illness
11. Known allergy or hypersensitivity to Levetiracetam or other pyrrolidone derivatives, or any of the excipients.
12. Known allergy or hypersensitivity to microcrystalline cellulose or lactose
13. Being under legal protection
